clue.text: Catches fish in special nets

indicators.note: in tells us the fishing verb sits inside the rearranged letters
special suggests the word nets made into something out of the ordinary, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: to fish with a rod and line is to angle

explanation.surface: An angler or trawlerman lands a catch using purpose-made nets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fish' looks like a noun in the surface, but it is the verb, sitting inside the shuffled nets.
explanation.definitionFit: To entangle is to snare or trap, as one catches something in a net.

clue.text: Spirit shown by those finally getting to the top

indicators.note: in a down clue the top is the start, so the final letter of the word those climbs to the front

explanation.surface: Team spirit is displayed by the people who finally make it to the summit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally getting to the top' takes the last letter, E, of THOSE and moves it to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: An ethos is the characteristic spirit or guiding beliefs of a group or culture.

clue.text: Informal chat at a board meeting

definitions.text: Informal chat at a board meeting

parts.words: Informal chat at a board meeting
parts.note: a board is a dining table, so this is relaxed conversation over a meal rather than a company board's business

explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a company's boardroom, but the board here is the old word for a dining table.
explanation.definitionFit: Conversation held over a meal is casual dinner-party chat, the kind recorded in collections of famous people's sayings.

clue.text: Disreputable degenerate held up by no promises to pay

indicators.note: in a down clue, held up means the word is lifted so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: to degenerate is to rot or decay
an IOU is a written promise to pay a debt, plural IOUS

explanation.surface: A disreputable wastrel is propped up by nothing more than unpaid debts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held up' turns ROT into TOR in this down clue, giving NO-TOR-IOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone notorious is famous for bad reasons, having a shady reputation.

clue.text: Rocky island with nowhere to relax

indicators.note: rocky means unsteady or shaky, telling us the letters that follow are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A craggy, barren island offers no place to unwind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rocky' looks like a description of the island, but it signals rearranging ISLAND, NOWHERE and TO together; 'with' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for unwinding and abandoning formality pictures freeing one's tied-up locks.

clue.text: Send on part of course at the outset that's undemanding

parts.words: part of course at the outset
parts.note: a straight is a level stretch of a racecourse; at the outset says this piece comes first
to send on a letter is to forward it

explanation.surface: An instruction about rerouting mail or a race lap, then a remark that the task is easy.
explanation.walkthrough: A STRAIGHT is the straight section of a racecourse, such as the home straight.
explanation.definitionFit: A task that is simple and uncomplicated is described as easy to carry out, without hidden difficulty.

clue.text: Fired workers united in display of insolence

indicators.note: in places the workers' group inside the word for cheek

parts.note: lip is slang for cheeky, impertinent talk
TU stands for trade union, a body of workers united

explanation.surface: Sacked staff band together and show open defiance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fired' suggests dismissal, but the definition means set alight or illuminated.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that has been ignited or illuminated is set alight, as a fire or a lamp is.

clue.text: Time to enter Euro-currency in some measure

indicators.note: to enter tells us the time abbreviation goes inside the currency word

parts.note: lire, plural of lira, were the currency of Italy, a European country

explanation.surface: It is time a common European currency was brought in to some extent.
explanation.walkthrough: The lira was Italy's currency before the euro; 'Euro-currency' means a European one, not the euro.
explanation.definitionFit: A metric unit of liquid volume, roughly a quart, is one example of a measure.

clue.text: Short length of intersection

indicators.note: a length of a word is a stretch of its letters, so the answer sits within the clue word intersection

explanation.surface: A brief stretch of road at a crossroads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short length' looks like one phrase, but 'Short' is the definition and 'length of' points into inTERSEction.
explanation.definitionFit: A curt or brief reply uses few words, so it is clipped and concise.

clue.text: Cheese and wine getting a lot of recognition

parts.note: port is a fortified wine from Portugal

indicators.note: a lot of means most but not all, so the last letter of the recognition word is dropped

parts.note: a salute is a gesture of recognition

explanation.surface: Cheese and wine served to a round of applause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' drops the final E from SALUTE, giving SALUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A mild semi-soft French variety made originally by Trappist monks is one kind of dairy product from milk curds.

clue.text: Living space a little restricted in Derby, say

indicators.note: restricted in means the small amount is confined inside the headgear

parts.note: a derby is a bowler hat, so it is an example of headwear
a little means a bit

explanation.surface: A cramped room in the English city of Derby.
explanation.walkthrough: Derby looks like the English city, but a derby is also a bowler hat; 'say' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The natural home where an animal or plant lives is its environment, a living space.

clue.text: He leaves engineers to fit exhaust before run

indicators.note: before places the exhaust word ahead of the run abbreviation

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
to exhaust someone is to tire them
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A mechanic fits a new exhaust pipe and then takes a car for a run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exhaust' suggests a car part, but it is the verb meaning wear out; 'to fit' only links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who withdraws or goes to bed early is one who departs, so a person who leaves.

clue.text: Guide animal

definitions.meaning: to guide a vehicle or a course is to direct it
a young castrated bull, raised for beef

explanation.surface: A guide dog or other helper animal.
explanation.definitionFit: One verb sense is to direct a course; the noun sense is a bullock reared for meat.

clue.text: Quiet, without hooter going about one

indicators.note: going about means wrapping around, so the nose word surrounds the numeral

parts.note: hooter is slang for the nose
I is the Roman numeral one
less means lacking, as a suffix meaning without

explanation.surface: Peace and quiet with no car horn sounding around anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hooter' looks like a car horn but is slang for nose; LESS follows as the suffix meaning without.
explanation.definitionFit: Something silent makes no sound at all.

clue.text: Tough lawman having occasion to trap drivers

indicators.note: to trap means to hold captive within, so the party word encloses the motorists' club

parts.note: a do is a party or social occasion
the RAC, Royal Automobile Club, is a British motorists' organisation

explanation.surface: A hard-line policeman uses an event as a chance to catch speeding motorists.
explanation.walkthrough: The RAC is a British motoring organisation like the American AAA. The answer is the ancient Athenian lawgiver whose harsh laws gave us 'draconian'.
explanation.definitionFit: This Athenian legislator was famous for harsh laws, so he was a severe lawgiver.

clue.text: Precipitated advance in action

indicators.note: in places the word for proposing inside the word for a deed

parts.note: a deed is an action
to advance an idea is to posit or put it forward

explanation.surface: A sudden step forward in a battle or lawsuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'advance' looks like a military move or payment but means put forward an idea.
explanation.definitionFit: Chemists say a solid precipitated from a solution is laid down, settled as sediment.

clue.text: A rerouting of his parcel round

indicators.note: a rerouting sends something by a different way, so the letters of the two words travel into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone's package gets sent the long way round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' looks like a route word in the surface, but it is the adjective meaning ball-shaped.
explanation.definitionFit: Something shaped like a ball or globe is round.

clue.text: Gives further attention to a learner's practice session

parts.note: to re-hear a case is to give it further attention, as a court does
L stands for learner, as on British L-plates for learner drivers

explanation.surface: An instructor goes over a learner driver's practice session again.
explanation.walkthrough: L is the learner's letter from British L-plates on cars driven by learners.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial run of a performance before the real thing is a practice session.

clue.text: One performs rite as church supporter in period of penance

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: in places the supporting garment inside the season of penance

parts.note: Lent is the Christian season of fasting and penance before Easter
a bra is a supporting undergarment

explanation.surface: Someone conducting a ceremony also supports the church during Lent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporter' looks like a churchgoer but is the undergarment; CE is the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: A priest officiating at a religious ceremony, especially the Eucharist, is the person conducting it.

clue.text: Take rod to fish — that's plain

indicators.note: to means added to, so the rod word joins the end of the fish

parts.note: the pike is a freshwater fish
a staff is a rod or stick

explanation.surface: An angler is told to bring a rod for fishing, because the method is obvious.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'plain as a pikestaff' means obvious; 'Take' only introduces the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom plain as a pikestaff makes the old spear shaft a byword for something obvious.

clue.text: Man taking on many an old serf

indicators.note: taking on means adding, so the word for many follows the pronoun

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man
a lot means many

explanation.surface: A man takes on a large number of jobs, like a medieval serf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' gives the pronoun HE rather than a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Sparta, the state-owned bonded labourers were a class of serf.

clue.text: Source of spiteful burden Queen placed on Snow White, perhaps

indicators.note: placed on means the Queen abbreviation is added to the end
the source of a word is where it begins, so its first letter is taken

parts.note: to lumber someone is to burden them
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: The wicked Queen in the fairy tale lays a spiteful curse on Snow White.
explanation.walkthrough: In the fairy tale Snow White falls into a long sleep after eating the Queen's poisoned apple; 'perhaps' marks her as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The heroine lies asleep under a spell, so she is an example of a sleeper.

clue.text: The taking of excess profit for accommodation

definitions.text: The taking of excess profit for accommodation

parts.words: The taking of excess profit for accommodation
parts.note: accommodation is an old financial word for a loan, so this means charging extortionate interest on lending, not overcharging for lodgings

explanation.walkthrough: 'accommodation' suggests a room or lodgings, but in old banking language it means a loan.
explanation.definitionFit: Charging exorbitant interest on a loan is exploitative money-lending.

clue.text: Fine Scottish leader in national show of strength

parts.note: braw is Scots for fine or good

indicators.note: the leader in a word is its first letter, so only the start of national is used

explanation.surface: A Scottish leader puts on a fine display of national power.
explanation.walkthrough: BRAW is a Scots word for fine or handsome.
explanation.definitionFit: Muscle and physical power are what one shows in a display of might.

clue.text: Opening move executed to gain room for manoeuvre

indicators.note: executed means beheaded, so the first letter is removed

parts.note: a gambit is an opening move in chess

explanation.surface: A chess opening is played to create space for tactics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'executed' looks like carried out, but it means beheaded: GAMBIT loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Scope or extent within which one can act is space to move freely.

clue.text: Had a revolution, ousting king, and restored harmony

indicators.note: ousting means throwing out, so the monarch letter is removed from the word

parts.note: to have turned is to have rotated, made a revolution
R, for rex, is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A country rose up, overthrew its monarch and brought back peace.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a political uprising, but a revolution is a turn; R (rex) is king.
explanation.definitionFit: An instrument that has been adjusted to the right pitch has had its harmony put right again.

clue.text: Travel firm recruiting ace flyer

indicators.note: recruiting means taking on board, so the travel-firm pair takes the ace letter into it

parts.note: to tour is to travel
CO is short for company, a firm
A is the abbreviation for ace in cards

explanation.surface: A holiday company hires a top pilot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flyer' suggests a pilot, but the answer is an African bird.
explanation.definitionFit: This colourful African bird is an example of a creature that flies.

clue.text: Decline to give bad mark to backward scholar

indicators.note: to means next to, so the mark follows the turned degree
backward means the scholar's degree letters are read in reverse

parts.note: a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate scholar
a stain is a blemish or bad mark

explanation.surface: A teacher declines to give a poor grade to a slow pupil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backward' looks like describing a slow pupil, but it reverses BA, giving AB.
explanation.definitionFit: To refrain, especially from voting, is to decline to take part.

clue.text: The old fellow outside is the most senior person

indicators.note: outside tells us the fellow word wraps around the old form of the

parts.note: a don is a fellow of a college
ye is an archaic form of the

explanation.surface: An old man waiting outside turns out to be the eldest of the group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The old fellow' looks like one phrase, but 'The old' gives YE and 'fellow' a university DON.
explanation.definitionFit: The senior member of a profession or group is its most respected elder.

clue.text: Showing lumps, being led out and mistreated

indicators.note: mistreated means handled badly, so the letters of the preceding words are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: Someone bruised after being dragged outside and abused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mistreated' rearranges LED OUT AND, with 'and' part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Having small rounded swellings or knots is having lumps, as a nodular growth does.
